text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The case of the "missing" 600 million ringgit from a rubber replanting fund was closed after the Cabinet accepted the explanation of two ministers that a newspaper report on the issue was unfounded.
-- The chief ministers of Malacca and Penang states issued new directives that state lawmakers must declare their assets, in a move to curb corruption.
-- AMMB Holdings Bhd joined the exclusive billion ringgit pre-tax profit club, posting 1.02 billion for the year ended March 31, 1997.

-- The Health Ministry has advised public swimming pools, nurseries and kindergartens to close temporarily in eastern Sarawak state in efforts to contain an airborne disease suspected to be caused by the coxsackie virus B.
